ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a voltage divider circuit. The externally applied total voltage U1 is marked on the left. In the vertical branch, R1 is above and R2 is below. The voltmeter V on the right is connected between the middle tap and the lower common node, so the voltmeter is in parallel with the lower-arm R2, and the U2 marked on the right is the lower-arm voltage measured by the voltmeter. Reasoning: The internal resistance of the voltmeter RV = 300 kΩ, and R2 = 300 kΩ, so the equivalent resistance of the lower arm is R2 || RV = 300 kΩ || 300 kΩ = 150 kΩ. The voltmeter reading is 180 V, that is, the voltage across the lower-arm equivalent resistance is U2 = 180 V. The series current I = 180 V / 150 kΩ = 1.2 mA. The voltage drop across R1 = 200 kΩ is UR1 = I R1 = 1.2 mA × 200 kΩ = 240 V. Therefore, the applied voltage U1 = UR1 + U2 = 240 V + 180 V = 420 V.
